title: Halloumi & Tomato Salad
description: Salty, griddled halloumi over ripe tomatoes with a sharp lemon-oil dressing — ready before the pan's even properly hot.
instructions: Slice the tomatoes and arrange them on a plate with the red onion.
Slice the halloumi into 1cm-thick pieces.
Heat a dry pan on high for a minute, then griddle the halloumi for 90 seconds a side, until it's dark gold and blistered.
Lay the halloumi over the tomatoes.
Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, and oregano, then pour it over everything. Eat immediately, while the halloumi's still squeaky.

title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: Garlic, chili, and good olive oil turned into a sauce by nothing but pasta water and patience. Five ingredients, no excuses.
instructions: Salt a big pot of water heavily and bring it to a boil. Cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente.
While it cooks, warm the olive oil in a large pan over low heat. Add the garlic and chili flakes and cook gently for 2-3 minutes — you want it soft and fragrant, not browned.
Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Tip the spaghetti into the pan with the garlic oil. Add a splash of the pasta water and toss hard over medium heat for a minute, until the sauce clings and turns glossy.
Stir through the parsley and serve straight away.

title: Greek Yoghurt with Honey & Walnuts
description: The five-minute breakfast every Greek grandmother has made a thousand times: thick yoghurt, good honey, toasted walnuts.
instructions: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl.
Scatter the walnuts over the top.
Drizzle with honey and a light dusting of cinnamon. Done.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, eaten straight from the pan with bread for mopping. A one-pan dinner that looks harder than it is.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the onion and pepper and cook for 6-8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, and paprika and cook for another minute.
Pour in the canned tomatoes and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens into a sauce.
Make four small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each one. Cover the pan and cook for 5-6 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with bread.

title: Ful Medames
description: Egypt's everyday breakfast — warm mashed fava beans with garlic, lemon, and olive oil. Cheap, filling, and better than it has any right to be.
instructions: Tip the fava beans and their liquid into a small pot. Warm them through over medium heat for 5 minutes, mashing about half of them with a fork as they heat.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, and half the lemon juice. Simmer for another 5 minutes, adding a splash of water if it looks dry.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with olive oil and the rest of the lemon juice.
Top with the diced tomato and parsley. Eat with warm bread.

title: Greek Village Salad (Horiatiki)
description: The classic village salad of Cyprus and Greece — ripe tomatoes, cool cucumber, sharp feta, and a drizzle of good olive oil. No lettuce, no frills.
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and the cucumber into thick half-moons. Slice the onion and pepper thinly.
Toss them together in a large bowl with the olives.
Place the block of feta on top whole — don't crumble it.
Drizzle with olive oil, scatter with oregano, and serve with bread to catch the juices.

title: Tzatziki with Warm Pita
description: Cold, garlicky cucumber yoghurt that cools down anything spicy next to it. Ten minutes of chopping, then it just sits and gets better.
instructions: Grate the cucumber, then squeeze it hard in a clean tea towel to get rid of as much water as you can — skip this and the tzatziki turns watery.
Mix the cucumber into the yoghurt with the garlic, dill, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt.
Stir in the olive oil. Cover and let it sit in the fridge for at least 20 minutes so the flavors settle.
Warm the pita in a dry pan for a minute a side and serve alongside.

title: Tabbouleh
description: This is a herb salad that happens to have some bulgur in it, not the other way round — parsley is the main event.
instructions: Cover the bulgur with boiling water and let it sit for 15 minutes, until tender. Drain well and let it cool.
Finely chop the parsley, mint, tomatoes, and onion — the finer the better, this isn't meant to be a chunky salad.
Mix the cooled bulgur through the chopped vegetables and herbs.
Dress with the lemon juice, olive oil, and a good pinch of salt. Taste and add more lemon if it needs it.

title: Moussaka
description: Layers of fried eggplant, spiced lamb, and a thick béchamel, baked until the top turns golden. The dish that makes people request seconds.
instructions: Salt the eggplant slices and let them sit for 20 minutes to draw out the bitterness, then pat them dry.
Fry the eggplant slices in olive oil until golden on both sides. Set aside on paper towel.
In the same pan, cook the onion and garlic until soft. Add the lamb mince and brown it, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, and cinnamon. Simmer for 15 minutes until it thickens into a ragu.
For the béchamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook for a minute. Gradually whisk in the milk until you have a smooth, thick sauce. Stir in half the parmesan.
Layer the eggplant and lamb ragu in a baking dish, finishing with the béchamel on top. Scatter the rest of the parmesan over it.
Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes, until the top is golden and bubbling. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting — it'll fall apart if you don't.

title: Lemon Roast Chicken
description: Chicken thighs roasted with lemon, garlic, and potatoes until the skin crisps and the potatoes soak up all the juices.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Toss the potato wedges and chicken thighs together in a roasting tray with the olive oil, oregano, salt, and a good grind of pepper.
Squeeze the juice of one lemon over everything, then cut the squeezed halves and the second lemon into wedges and tuck them into the tray along with the garlic cloves and rosemary.
Roast for 45-50 minutes, turning the potatoes halfway, until the chicken skin is crisp and the potatoes are golden.
Squeeze the roasted lemon wedges over the tray before serving.

title: Pasta al Limone
description: Butter, parmesan, and lemon zest turned into a sauce that clings to every strand. Looks fancy, takes fifteen minutes.
instructions: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente. Scoop out a mug of the pasta water before draining.
Melt the butter in a large pan over low heat. Add the lemon zest and juice and a splash of the pasta water.
Add the drained spaghetti to the pan and toss well.
Take the pan off the heat and add the parmesan a handful at a time, tossing constantly so it melts into a sauce instead of clumping.
Add more pasta water if it looks too thick. Finish with black pepper and torn basil.

title: Stuffed Peppers
description: Bell peppers packed with spiced rice and beef, baked until the peppers slump and the filling turns tender. Better the next day.
instructions: Slice the tops off the peppers and scoop out the seeds and membranes. Set the peppers upright in a baking dish.
Heat the oven to 190°C.
Cook the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft. Add the beef mince and brown it.
Stir in the rice, half the canned tomatoes, and a splash of water. Simmer for 5 minutes, then take off the heat and stir through the parsley.
Spoon the filling into the peppers. Pour the rest of the canned tomatoes over and around them.
Cover with foil and bake for 35 minutes, then uncover and bake for another 10 minutes so the tops color slightly.

title: Chicken Souvlaki
description: Skewered, marinated chicken grilled until charred at the edges. Cypriot summer food, no fancy equipment needed beyond a hot pan.
instructions: Mix the chicken with the lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, and oregano. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes — longer if you have the time.
Thread the chicken onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water first so they don't burn).
Grill or pan-fry the skewers over high heat for 10-12 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until charred and cooked through.
Meanwhile, stir the grated cucumber into the yoghurt with a pinch of salt for a quick dip.
Serve the skewers hot with the yoghurt on the side.

title: Chicken Shawarma Bowls
description: All the flavor of a shawarma wrap without needing a spit — spiced chicken over rice, with cool yoghurt to cut through the heat.
instructions: Mix the chicken with the cumin, paprika, garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil. Marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Cook the rice according to the pack instructions.
Heat a pan over high heat and cook the chicken in batches for 6-8 minutes, until well browned and cooked through.
Divide the rice between bowls. Top with the chicken, diced cucumber, and tomatoes.
Finish with a dollop of yoghurt over each bowl.

title: Falafel with Tahini Sauce
description: Crisp, herby chickpea patties with a lemony tahini sauce for dipping. Frying takes practice but the payoff is worth it.
instructions: Blitz the chickpeas, garlic, parsley, coriander, and cumin in a food processor until it forms a coarse, sticky paste — don't over-blend it into a purée.
Stir in the flour and shape the mixture into small patties.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Fry the patties for 3-4 minutes a side, until deep golden and crisp.
While they fry, whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and a splash of water until it turns pale and pourable.
Serve the falafel hot with the tahini sauce.

title: Baked Feta Pasta
description: A block of feta and a tray of cherry tomatoes roasted together until they collapse into a sauce, then stirred straight through pasta. Barely any effort for how good it looks.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Tip the cherry tomatoes into a baking dish, nestle the block of feta in the middle, and scatter the garlic cloves around it. Drizzle everything with the olive oil and the chili flakes.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the tomatoes have burst and the feta is soft and blistered on top.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Save a mug of the pasta water before draining.
Mash the feta and tomatoes together right in the baking dish, then stir in the drained pasta and a splash of pasta water until it comes together as a sauce.
Finish with torn basil.

title: Kleftiko
description: Lamb shoulder rubbed with garlic and lemon, sealed up, and left to slow-roast for hours until it falls apart at the touch of a fork. Mostly the oven's work, not yours.
instructions: Heat the oven to 150°C.
Cut small slits all over the lamb shoulder and push a sliver of garlic into each one.
Rub the lamb all over with olive oil, the juice of both lemons, and the oregano. Season well with salt.
Put the potatoes in the bottom of a large roasting tray, sit the lamb on top, and add the thyme sprigs and the squeezed lemon halves.
Cover the tray tightly with foil — this traps the steam and is what makes the lamb fall apart later.
Roast for 3.5 hours, then remove the foil and roast for another 20-30 minutes to brown the top.
Rest for 15 minutes before pulling the meat apart with two forks.

title: Spanakopita
description: Spinach and feta wrapped in paper-thin, buttery pastry. Working with phyllo takes a steady hand the first time, but it's just repetition after that.
instructions: Cook the onion in olive oil until soft. Add the spinach in batches and cook until wilted, then tip it into a colander and press out as much liquid as you can once it's cool enough to handle.
Mix the spinach and onion with the crumbled feta, eggs, and dill in a bowl.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Brush a baking dish with melted butter.
Lay one sheet of phyllo in the dish, brush with melted butter, and repeat with half the sheets, letting the edges hang over.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the pastry, then layer the remaining sheets on top, brushing each with butter.
Fold in the overhanging edges and score the top layer into portions with a sharp knife — this stops the whole thing shattering when you cut it later.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, until deep golden and crisp. Let it cool for 10 minutes before cutting along the scored lines.

title: Beef Stifado
description: A slow-cooked beef and shallot stew, sweetened with cinnamon and a good glug of red wine. It wants time more than attention — most of this is just waiting.
instructions: Brown the beef in batches in olive oil over high heat, then set aside.
In the same pot, brown the shallots whole until they pick up some color.
Return the beef to the pot with the garlic, bay leaves, and cinnamon stick. Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes to cook off the harshness.
Add the canned tomatoes and vinegar, then top up with enough water to just cover everything.
Cover and simmer on very low heat for 2-2.5 hours, checking occasionally, until the beef is fork-tender and the sauce has thickened.
Fish out the cinnamon stick and bay leaves before serving.

title: Lamb Kofta with Rice
description: Spiced lamb patties grilled on skewers over rice. The mix needs a firm hand to shape and a hot enough pan to char — get those two right and the rest is easy.
instructions: Squeeze the grated onion in a clean tea towel to remove excess water, then mix it into the lamb mince with the parsley, cumin, paprika, garlic, and a good pinch of salt.
Work the mixture with your hands for a couple of minutes until it feels tacky — this is what holds the kofta together on the skewer.
Shape into oval patties around skewers, pressing firmly.
Cook the rice according to the pack instructions.
Grill or pan-fry the kofta over high heat for 4-5 minutes a side, until charred outside and cooked through.
Serve over the rice with a spoon of yoghurt on the side.

title: Fattoush with Grilled Halloumi
description: A crunchy, sumac-dressed salad topped with fried pita chips and grilled halloumi. More chopping than skill, but there's a lot of chopping.
instructions: Tear or cut the pita into rough pieces and fry in a little olive oil until crisp and golden. Set aside on paper towel.
Chop the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, and radish and toss together in a large bowl with the mint.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, and sumac for the dressing.
Slice the halloumi and griddle it in a dry pan for about 90 seconds a side, until charred and soft in the middle.
Toss the salad with the dressing, then top with the fried pita and grilled halloumi. Serve right away, before the pita softens.

title: Pastitsio
description: Greece's answer to lasagne — tubed pasta layered with a cinnamon-spiced meat sauce and a thick béchamel, baked until set. A weekend project, not a weeknight one.
instructions: Cook the pasta until just shy of al dente, drain, and set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic until soft, then add the beef mince and brown it well.
Stir in the canned tomatoes, tomato paste, and cinnamon. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.

For the béchamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook for a minute. Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth and thick. Take off the heat, cool slightly, then beat in the eggs and half the parmesan.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Layer the pasta and meat sauce in a baking dish, then pour the béchamel over the top and scatter with the rest of the parmesan.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, until the top is set and deeply golden. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting — it needs that time to hold together.

title: Chicken Musakhan
description: Roast chicken over sumac-soaked flatbread, piled with sweet caramelized onions and toasted pine nuts. A Palestinian classic built for sharing straight off the tray.
instructions: Toss the chicken with half the olive oil, half the sumac, the lemon juice, and a good pinch of salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the sliced onions in the rest of the olive oil over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft, sweet, and deeply golden. Stir in the remaining sumac.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Lay the pita breads in a large roasting tray and spoon half the caramelized onions over them.
Sit the chicken on top of the onion-covered bread and roast for 35-40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the bread underneath has soaked up the juices.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for a minute or two until golden — watch them closely, they burn fast.
Top the tray with the rest of the onions and the toasted pine nuts before serving.

title: Lamb Tagine with Apricots
description: Lamb slow-braised with warm spices and dried apricots until it's soft enough to eat with a spoon. The kind of dish that's better the day after.
instructions: Brown the lamb in batches in olive oil over high heat, then set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onion and garlic until soft.
Return the lamb to the pot with the cinnamon and cumin. Stir for a minute until fragrant.
Add the dried apricots, honey, and chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 1.5-2 hours, checking occasionally and topping up with water if it looks dry, until the lamb is completely tender.
